skills.name: Three-pass reading
skills.description: Read a paper in three passes of increasing depth, stopping when you have what you need.

skills.name: Paper cards
skills.description: Capture each paper's question, method, result with size and uncertainty, limitation and your own critique on one card.

skills.name: Literature search
skills.description: Find the key papers on a topic using search engines, citation trails and reference lists.

skills.name: Field map
skills.description: Organise about thirty papers into groups that show the main ideas, debates and gaps in a field.

skills.name: Reading figures and tables
skills.description: Work out what a figure or table shows, including axes, units, error bars and sample sizes, before reading the text about it.

skills.name: Critical appraisal
skills.description: Judge whether a paper's claims are supported by its design, data and analysis.

skills.name: Reading statistics
skills.description: Interpret effect sizes, confidence intervals and p-values correctly and spot common misuses.

skills.name: Choosing important problems
skills.description: Judge whether a problem is important, open and within reach before committing time to it.

skills.name: Framing a research question
skills.description: Turn a broad interest into a specific question that a study could answer.

skills.name: Forming hypotheses
skills.description: State a testable hypothesis and the prediction that would show it to be wrong.

skills.name: Operationalising constructs
skills.description: Choose measures that capture the concept you care about, and argue for their validity.

skills.name: Spotting confounds
skills.description: Identify third variables and alternative explanations that could produce a result.

skills.name: Causal reasoning
skills.description: Judge what kind of design is needed to support a claim about cause and effect.

skills.name: Reasoning under uncertainty
skills.description: Weigh evidence by its strength and state conclusions with honest uncertainty.

skills.name: Study design
skills.description: Choose a design, conditions, sample and measures that can answer the research question.

skills.name: Baselines and ablations
skills.description: Compare against fair baselines and remove components to find out what drives a result.

skills.name: Sample size planning
skills.description: Use a power analysis or other justification to decide how much data to collect.

skills.name: Preregistering a study
skills.description: Write down hypotheses, design and analysis plan before collecting or examining data.

skills.name: Data analysis
skills.description: Clean, explore and analyse data, keeping planned and exploratory analyses clearly apart.

skills.name: Reproducible pipeline
skills.description: Build an analysis that someone else can rerun from raw data to final figures.

skills.name: Running a project
skills.description: Carry a project from question to published result, adjusting plans as evidence comes in.

skills.name: Research note-taking
skills.description: Keep dated, searchable notes on what you read, did and decided.

skills.name: Writing an abstract
skills.description: Summarise question, method, main result with its size and conclusion in one short paragraph.

skills.name: Structuring a paper
skills.description: Organise a paper so each section does its job and the argument is easy to follow.

skills.name: Writing related work
skills.description: Place your study among prior work and make clear what is new.

skills.name: Hedging claims
skills.description: Match the strength of every claim to the strength of its evidence.

skills.name: Figure design
skills.description: Make figures with clear axes, honest scales and captions that stand on their own.

skills.name: Responding to reviewers
skills.description: Answer each reviewer comment politely and specifically, with changes or reasoned disagreement.

skills.name: Writing a proposal
skills.description: Write a research or funding proposal that states the problem, approach, risks and measures of success.

skills.name: Research vocabulary
skills.description: Use core research terms correctly and naturally in speech.

skills.name: Discussing research
skills.description: Talk about research ideas and findings clearly with a supervisor or peer.

skills.name: Presenting a paper
skills.description: Present someone else's paper to a group, covering its claim, evidence and weaknesses.

skills.name: Answering questions
skills.description: Answer questions directly, say what you do not know, and avoid defensive replies.

skills.name: Research pitch
skills.description: Explain your research and why it matters in under a minute to a non-specialist.

skills.name: Conference talk
skills.description: Give a timed talk on your own work with a clear take-home message.

skills.name: Handling critique
skills.description: Defend your work under hard questioning while conceding valid points.

skills.name: How research works
skills.description: Explain the research cycle, the roles in a lab and how work moves from idea to publication.

skills.name: Learning how to learn
skills.description: Use retrieval practice and spaced repetition to keep what you study.

skills.name: Reference management
skills.description: Keep every source in a reference manager with notes and tags from the first day.

skills.name: Keeping a lab notebook
skills.description: Record work, decisions and failures at the time they happen.

skills.name: Version control
skills.description: Track changes to code and text so any result can be traced to the version that made it.

skills.name: Data management
skills.description: Store, document, protect and share data according to a written plan.

skills.name: Ethics process
skills.description: Prepare an ethics application, consent materials and data protection measures before a study starts.

skills.name: Peer reviewing
skills.description: Write a fair, specific and useful review of another researcher's manuscript.

skills.name: Project planning
skills.description: Plan a year of research with milestones, risks and checks on progress.
